title: Japji 8–15, whole

segments.voice: Yesterday, walk in the order: Japji pauris one to seven, held by one thread. The next eight have a beat you can hear.
screen: `WALK IN THE ORDER.` → `NOW, A BEAT YOU CAN HEAR.`

segments.voice: A chorus at a game, a refrain at a wedding: after the second time, you know where it's going before it lands. Pauri eight of the Japji does that. Suniai, it begins: by listening. Pauri nine: suniai. Ten: suniai. Eleven: suniai. Then the word changes, and the next four begin mannai: by trusting. So, one question for today: why does listening come first?
screen: `A CHORUS YOU SEE COMING.` → `SUNIAI, SUNIAI, SUNIAI, SUNIAI.` → `THEN MANNAI. WHY LISTEN FIRST?`

segments.voice: The suniai pauris pile up what listening does: by listening, the adepts and the holy came to be; by listening, the blind find the way. Each one ends on the same refrain: Nanak bhagataa sadaa vigaas, suniai dookh paap kaa naas. The devotees are always in bloom; by listening, pain and wrong are gone. Then the mannai pauris turn to what comes after hearing: trusting, taking it in. Guru Nanak says the state of the one who trusts can't be told; there's no paper or pen for it. By trusting, awareness wakes; the path opens; the door of freedom is found. So the Japji's answer comes in an order: listen, then trust. Now a neighbor, in its own words. Paul, writing to the Christians in Rome, says something that rhymes. In the King James Bible: "So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God." Shared ground: trust doesn't start with effort; it starts with the ears. And one honest difference. Paul means hearing the message about Christ, preached and believed. Guru Nanak means listening to the Name itself, a listening that changes the listener, and a trust he says no words can reach.
screen: `SUNIAI: BY LISTENING.` · `MANNAI: BY TRUSTING.` · `ROMANS: FAITH COMETH BY HEARING.` · `SHARED EARS, DIFFERENT WORD.` · then, large: `LISTEN, TRUST.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and choose one sound in the room: a fan, the traffic, your own breath. Just listen to it, without naming it or judging it. When your mind wanders off, come back to the listening, as many times as it takes.
Japji 8. Pauris eight to fifteen, read whole: four that begin suniai, by listening, and four that begin mannai, by trusting.
For the road: listen, trust, in that order, the ears first and then the yes. Three of the summit.

notes: 2026-10-15 v3 written: shape wisdom. Question: why does listening come first? Sikh answer: pauris 8-11 (suniai) and 12-15 (mannai) in that order. Answers day 1762's question (the word is suniai); tomorrow's question (the Japji starts to count) is answered by day 1764's hook (asankh).

Unity thread (weekly): neighbor = Christianity, Romans 10:17 (KJV), 'So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.' Shared ground: trust begins with hearing. Honest difference: Paul means hearing the message about Christ preached (Romans 10:14-17); the Japji means listening to the Name, and calls the trusting state beyond words. No ranking; the chat's and myth's 'exactly the same' options are there to catch that. Confirm a Christian reader finds it fair.

The counts ('four that begin suniai', 'the next four begin mannai') are read off the cited text itself (pauris 8-11 and 12-15). Pauri 8's 'adepts and the holy' paraphrases suniai sidh peer sur naath; pauri 11 'the blind find the way' is suniai andhe paavahi raahu. Confirm.
